sq.QUESTION_DESC: 1) Differentiate between logical address space and physical address space.

sq.ANSWER:
Address binding is the process of mapping logical addresses (used by programs) to physical addresses (used by hardware).
There are three types of address binding:

  1. Compile-time binding – if memory location is known at compile time.

  2. Load-time binding – if address is determined at program load.

  3. Execution-time binding – if address changes during execution (used in dynamic memory allocation).

sq.QUESTION_DESC: 1)Define address binding. What are the types of address binding?

lq.ANSWER:
Definition of Address Binding: (20%)

Address binding is the process of mapping logical addresses (also known as virtual addresses) to physical addresses (actual memory locations in RAM).

When a program is executed, the CPU generates addresses during instruction execution. These addresses must be translated to actual locations in main memory — and this is done through address binding.

🔹 Types of Address Binding:

There are three main types of address binding, based on when the binding takes place:

1. Compile-Time Binding (20%)

  • Occurs when the program is compiled.

  • If the memory location is known in advance, the absolute physical address is embedded in the code.

  • ❌ Not flexible; cannot be relocated once compiled.

  • 📌 Example: Embedded systems.

2. Load-Time Binding (20%)

  • Used when it is not known where the program will be loaded into memory.

  • The compiler generates relocatable code.

  • The actual address is determined when the program is loaded into memory.

  • ✅ Allows relocation within memory at load time.

3. Execution-Time Binding (20%)

  • Binding occurs during execution.

  • The CPU generates logical addresses, which are converted to physical addresses on the fly by the Memory Management Unit (MMU).

  • ✅ Required for dynamic memory management and virtual memory systems.

  • Most modern systems use this.
